messages.author: 5140016d70f6ba82
messages.subject: Re: pooling or not pooling f(0)
parts:
I clarified off-list that there are just 2 observers - one on each side
of the plane.

One further question. Do you also have different spatial strata that
are not equally sampled? If you do not, then I think you are making
this too difficult.
All you need to do is setup year as the stratification variable and look
at MCDS models say ~1 (NULL), ~Observer, ~Year ~Observer+Year and
~Observer*Year. Then compute
an estimate of abundance/density for each year with the global detection
function option. Presumably you want a separate estimate for each
year. The only difficulty will be that unless the model is
~Year or ~Observer*Year then your yearly estimates have a covariance due
to the commonality of the detection function model. The model ~Observer
is pooled over years. The model ~Observer+Year has an additive effect
of year and observer. The model ~Observer*Year would be equivalent to
fitting the ~Observer model for each year separately. If you fit
~Observer*Year and estimate abundance for each year and then select each
year and fit ~Observer, then the results for each year should be the
same and the sum of the AICs for the detection functions for each year
should match the AIC from the pooled analysis with ~Observer*Year as
long as you use the same key function and have no adjustment functions.

--jeff
